sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'canceled' LIMIT 1000
SELECT c.customer_state, COUNT(*) FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c USING (customer_id) GROUP BY 1 LIMIT 1000
SELECT t.product_category_name_english, ROUND(AVG(p.product_weight_g), 1) FROM products AS p JOIN category_translation AS t USING (product_category_name) GROUP BY 1 LIMIT 1000

SELECT t.product_category_name_english AS category, ROUND(SUM(oi.price), 2) AS revenue FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o USING (order_id) JOIN products AS p USING (product_id) JOIN category_translation AS t USING (product_category_name) WHERE NOT o.order_status IN ('canceled', 'unavailable') GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY revenue DESC, category LIMIT 10

SELECT c.customer_state, ROUND(SUM(oi.price), 2) FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o USING (order_id) JOIN customers AS c USING (customer_id) WHERE NOT o.order_status IN ('canceled', 'unavailable') GROUP BY 1 LIMIT 1000

SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT oi.seller_id FROM order_items AS oi JOIN order_reviews AS r USING (order_id) GROUP BY 1 HAVING AVG(r.review_score) < (SELECT AVG(review_score) FROM order_reviews)) LIMIT 1000
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT c.customer_unique_id FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o USING (customer_id) GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) > 1) LIMIT 1000

WITH m AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS month, SUM(oi.price) AS revenue FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS oi USING (order_id) WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' GROUP BY 1) SELECT month, revenue, ROUND(100.0 * (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month)) / LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS mom_growth_pct FROM m ORDER BY month LIMIT 1000

WITH r AS (SELECT s.seller_state, s.seller_id, ROUND(SUM(oi.price), 2) AS revenue FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o USING (order_id) JOIN sellers AS s USING (seller_id) WHERE NOT o.order_status IN ('canceled', 'unavailable') GROUP BY 1, 2), k AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY seller_state ORDER BY revenue DESC, seller_id) AS rn FROM r) SELECT seller_state, seller_id, revenue FROM k WHERE rn = 1 LIMIT 1000

SELECT c.customer_state, ROUND(AVG(DATE_DIFF('DAY', o.order_purchase_timestamp, o.order_delivered_customer_date)), 1) AS avg_days FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c USING (customer_id) WHERE NOT o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NULL GROUP BY 1 LIMIT 1000
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date LIMIT 1000
